comment: meta-factory's own commissioned lanes (#193). The owner commissioned four instrument lanes on 2026-09-27 -- ledger, questions, pacemakers, methodology -- each owning one template instrument's development and cross-member deployment. They resolve through registry/factories/meta-factory.json's `lanes` (threads 3981 / 4087 / 4223 / 4186), so the derived actor is the role name below. Membership alone would have left them REFUSED: known_actors() reads this file's `actors` list, and authorized_for_event() unions `by_event` onto the core matrix, so a lane declared for membership and absent here for authorization resolves and is then refused BY NAME -- which is the better error and the point of #193. THE SET IS UNIFORM ON PURPOSE: the four lanes do the same kind of work (take a unit, settle it, report), and a differentiated set would encode a distinction no measurement supports. NOT GRANTED, and each for a stated reason: `intake` and `dispatch` are Triage's rows (SKILL.md section 4), `ruling` is the process owner's, `score` is Surveys' measurement duty, `genesis` is bootstrap-only. A lane that files a board item therefore still owes Triage its intake leg -- the delegation of work does not move the routing. EXTENDED 2026-09-28 (#209): fleet-instruments, review-rotation and insights join on the SAME uniform set and for the same reason the original four did — they take a unit, settle it and report. #209 named one lane; the artifact showed three: all three hold LIVE bindings in the Factories chat whose roles appear in no fragment, so the ledger refused every row each one wrote. The set is identical by construction, not by omission. EXTENDED 2026-09-28 (#210): the `release` event joins THE SAME SEVEN-LANE SET on a PRINCIPLE rather than a habit -- a lane may release the claim it may make, because a withdrawal is the mirror of a taking and the two legs must carry the same population or a claim lawfully taken cannot be lawfully withdrawn. The event stays OFF the core tuple (it is DECLARED in docs/ledger-refs-kinds.json), so the core vocabulary is unchanged; the vacuity pin in tests/test_ledger_schema.py is what makes this line obligatory rather than optional, and it fired on the declaration within the hour. NOT GRANTED, unchanged: `intake` and `dispatch` are Triage's rows (SKILL.md section 4), `ruling` is the process owner's, `score` is Surveys' measurement duty, `genesis` is bootstrap-only. EXTENDED 2026-10-03 (#283): `hygiene` joins on the SAME uniform set and for the same reason - the lane WRITES the hygiene instrument (docs/instruments/hygiene.md:6 names it as the authoring lane) and must be able to take and settle the units that instrument's law dispatches to it. It appeared in no fragment, no membership list and no authorization, so the ledger refused every row it wrote; the defect was latent only because the lane had not yet needed one. NOT GRANTED, unchanged: `intake` and `dispatch` are Triage's rows (SKILL.md section 4), `ruling` is the process owner's, `score` is Surveys' measurement duty, `genesis` is bootstrap-only. EXTENDED 2026-10-10 (#67, ruling n=1599): `conversion` joins THE SAME EIGHT-LANE SET on the same mirror principle `release` joined on -- a lane may DECLARE the conversion of the regression it may claim and close, because the row that answers a regression is the row that settles the unit, and a conversion the settling lane may not write would be a regression no lane may answer. The event stays OFF the core tuple (DECLARED in docs/ledger-refs-kinds.json), and the vacuity pin in tests/test_ledger_schema.py is what makes this line obligatory rather than optional: it fired on the declaration the moment it landed. CORRECTED 2026-10-10 (#67, ruling n=1599, procedure section 5.4): that extension named only the DECLARED lanes, and `conversion` is a DECLARED event -- it has no row in the core authorization matrix -- so this declaration is its ENTIRE population and every core lane was silently excluded. Measured: `surveys` was refused BY NAME at the append, so the run the ruling names as the declarer could not write the row its own leg reads; the repair had carried the join and nothing able to answer it, and zero `conversion` rows existed in the ledger 12 days after the ruling. The core claim-and-close lanes (hq, triage, worker, carrier, delegate, surveys) now join the set, applying the mirror principle above LITERALLY: a lane may declare the conversion of the regression it may claim and close. A declared event's `by_event` entry must name the FULL population, because there is no core row to fall back on. The same shape is present on `release`, the OTHER declared event: its entry names the eight instrument lanes and excludes all six lanes the core matrix authorizes to CLAIM, so a claim lawfully taken cannot be lawfully withdrawn by the lane that took it (0 release rows in 3085, 12 days after #210). Filed as board #461 and NOT fixed here, because it is a separate unit of work on the same defect class. RESOLVED 2026-10-11 (#461, ruling n=3091): the note above filed the `release` half rather than fixing it. It is now fixed. `release` is a DECLARED event, so its `by_event` entry is its ENTIRE population, and that population named only the eight instrument lanes -- none of the six lanes the core matrix authorizes to CLAIM could withdraw a claim it had lawfully taken. Measured before this repair: 373 claim rows against 0 release rows in 3085, twelve days after #210 declared the event. The core claim-and-close lanes (hq, triage, worker, carrier, delegate, surveys) now join `release`, making it the same fourteen-lane population `conversion` carries -- the mirror principle applied literally in both directions: a lane may withdraw the claim it may make. The event stays OFF the core tuple (DECLARED in docs/ledger-refs-kinds.json). The vacuity pin in tests/test_ledger_schema.py could not see this defect and is not claimed to: it catches an event that authorizes NOBODY, while `release` authorized eight -- a pin built to catch emptiness cannot see incompleteness, which is why the arm for that class was filed separately and is now LANDED as #526: `tests/test_declared_event_population.py` asserts, for EVERY declared event, that its `by_event` population is a SUPERSET of `claim`'s, and it carries its own hermetic bite pair so a population that happens to be right today cannot read as a working check. It is the gate that would have caught both #462 and #461, neither of which was found by a gate.
